summary: Installation is specified in near-implementable detail, but the ADR contradicts itself on whether reinstalling over locally edited vendored source refuses or replaces, and the tap operations lack name rules, codes and cache semantics.

questions.text: Should a repeat install over a locally edited vendored package refuse or replace it?
questions.reason: Decides whether the installer needs edit detection and a new refusal code; the Decision says replace with no force flag, but Verification says refuse destructive replacement of local source edits.

questions.text: Do the package exclusions (.git, .kyyn, dist-newstyle, .stack-work) apply only at the package root or at any depth?
questions.reason: Changes which files are vendored, which block install as uncommitted, and review diffs; the ADR lists the names as 'directories/entries' without a matching scope.

questions.text: Should a tap-qualified install refuse when the catalogue entry name differs from the fetched manifest name?
questions.reason: The manifest name sets the installed name, so a mismatch could replace an unrelated package; the ADR only says the qualified selection resolves to the existing PluginSource.

questions.text: Is plugin removal in scope, with what command, and what happens to instance configuration referencing the removed plugin?
questions.reason: Decides refuse/cascade/dangle behaviour touching ADR 0016 config; the ADR only says removals follow the evolution-owned route and defines no remove operation.

questions.text: What stable diagnostic codes apply to tap, search and guide failures?
questions.reason: Scripts and tests will depend on invented codes; the refusal table covers installation only, and guides/unsynced taps just get an unnamed 'actionable diagnostic'.

questions.text: What are the validation rules for tap names, duplicate taps or catalogue entries, a missing taps.dhall and catalogue source forms?
questions.reason: Tap names become .kyyn/taps/<name>/ paths and qualifiers split on '/'; the ADR shows the file shapes but gives no name grammar, duplicate rule or missing-file behaviour.

questions.text: What side effects do tap add, tap remove and a partially failing tap update have on the cache?
questions.reason: Decides sync-on-add, cache deletion on remove, per-tap failure reporting and pruning; the ADR says only that add/remove edit taps.dhall and update shallow-fetches.

questions.text: Which directory does the staged exchange swap, where does instance configuration live, and what holds after a crash mid-swap?
questions.reason: source/ and origin.dhall are siblings, so swapping them separately can pair new source with old origin; the ADR says stage before exchanging and promises atomicity only for validation failures, not interruption.

questions.text: How do plugins register health/description methods and methods not attached to a connector, given only a connectors export?
questions.reason: Shapes the entry-module contract, PreparedPackage and dispatch; the ADR says they share one registration mechanism but the only registration shown has no field for them.

questions.text: Should the manifest decoder refuse or ignore fields beyond name and entryModule?
questions.reason: Strict decoding breaks older releases on new fields, lenient decoding hides typos; the ADR gives only the 'initial shape'.

questions.text: Should an https source containing userinfo, a query or a fragment be refused, normalised or recorded verbatim?
questions.reason: The URL is persisted in committed origin.dhall, so embedded tokens would leak into KB history; the ADR supports only 'unauthenticated https' without saying how credentials in the URL are handled.

questions.text: What does PackageIdentity consist of: source byte hash, origin revision, toolchain identity or a combination?
questions.reason: It keys compiled artifacts and bindings; the ADR requires changed source or toolchain never select old artifacts but does not define the identity.

questions.text: Does a tap-qualified install use the synced tap revision or a fresh fetch of the source's default HEAD?
questions.reason: Decides offline install, which bytes are installed and whether a previewed guide matches; the synced-revision rule is stated only for guide reads.

questions.text: Does the saved review comparison count origin-only changes, and what is its persisted shape?
questions.reason: The comparison is persisted with candidate and accepted reports; the ADR lists its contents (added/removed/changed, origins, changed paths) but no schema or origin-only rule.

questions.text: For a local source, which code applies when --path is missing on disk versus present on disk but absent from HEAD?
questions.reason: Sets check order and reported code; the table maps an absent local directory to plugin.source-unavailable while the Git paragraph maps an absent --path to git.missing-subtree.

questions.text: What does plugin search match, and how does it behave when only some taps are synced or valid?
questions.reason: Changes result type and exit status; the ADR says only that search reads downloaded catalogues and unsynced taps report how to sync.
